Distinguish this from 「〜わけがない」(there is absolutely no way that...), which expresses complete negation. 「〜わけではない」often appears with words such as 「必ずしも」(not necessarily), 「すべて」(all), and 「いつも」(always).

The pattern 「～か～ないかのうちに」describes an action that has just begun—or may not even have finished—when the following action occurs immediately.
default.q.test-15-q11-11.explanation: The grammar pattern 「V-る / V-た ＋ か ＋ V-ない ＋ かのうちに」 combines the dictionary or past form of a verb with its negative form. It describes one event occurring so suddenly that another event follows immediately, before the first has clearly finished. It therefore means “just as...,” “no sooner had... than...,” or “before the first event had even ended, the second occurred.” Example: 「ベルが鳴るか鳴らないかのうちに、生徒たちは教室を飛び出した。」(No sooner had the bell rung than the students rushed out of the classroom.) The key feature is the paired affirmative and negative forms of the same verb, emphasizing immediate succession. The following clause is objective and must not contain a command or the speaker's volition.

In Japanese, the particle 「こそ」 gives special emphasis to the noun or reason immediately before it, meaning “precisely” or “exactly.”

It carries a strong, formal emphasis and is often used to express gratitude, determination, or a uniquely decisive cause. A common study-related example is「今年こそJLPT N2に合格してみせる」, meaning "This year, I will definitely pass JLPT N2!" Do not confuse it with patterns indicating scope, such as「にわたって」(throughout), or topic and relation, such as「に関して」(concerning). Remember that the core function of「こそ」is to put a spotlight on one particular element and emphasize it decisively.

For comparison with the abstract usage commonly seen on the N2, consider: 「マニュアルに沿って、機械を正しく操作してください」 (Please operate the machine correctly according to the manual). The most easily confused point is the difference between 「〜に沿って」 and 「〜に基づいて」 (based on) in choice (d). Remember that 「〜に沿って」 emphasizes proceeding alongside and closely following a predetermined path without deviating, whereas 「〜に基づいて」 treats a document, data, or rule as the foundation for making a judgment or developing something new.

Do not confuse it with the causal pattern 「〜ものだから」 or the conjectural forms 「〜そう」 and 「〜らしい」.

The pattern 「〜もかまわず」 comes from 構う (kamau, “to care about” or “to mind”) and describes acting without paying any attention to surrounding factors.

The following clause usually describes an actual action that is surprising, unexpected, or mildly blameworthy, so it should never be used for a command, request, or personal intention. default.q.test-53-q2-2.verdict:

default.q.test-53-q3-3.verdict:

The pattern V-ます stem + っぱなし describes leaving something in the state resulting from an action without taking the necessary follow-up step.

default.q.test-53-q4-4.verdict:

The adjective 「うれしい」takes its connective form and combines correctly with 「〜てたまりません」to express overwhelming, uncontrollable happiness.

✅ Correct answer: (b) というより
The pattern 「A というより B」means “B would be more accurate than A,” and is used to make an observation or correct an expression for greater precision.

The complete sentence means: "That shop sells vegetables and fruit as well as medicine, so it is more like a supermarket than a pharmacy." default.q.test-53-q7-7.verdict:

The complete sentence translates as: "If I were watching a film by this director for the first time, which work should I start with?" default.q.test-53-q8-8.verdict:
